findings.description: In async retry_any.__ror__, the flatten check tests `isinstance(other, retry_all)` instead of `retry_any`. A retry_all on the left is spliced into a retry_any, which changes the logic.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `(a & b) | async_retry_any(c, d)`, where the left operand is a retry_all. The code returns `retry_any(a, b, c, d)`, which retries if any of a, b, c or d holds. The intended meaning is `(a and b) or c or d`. Retries then fire when only `a` is true, so retries happen when they should not.

findings.description: The async retry_all.__rand__ flatten check is correct, but the matching async retry_any.__ror__ is wrong because it uses retry_all, which suggests the two methods were copy-pasted.
findings.rationale: The copy-paste pattern across the two methods risks the same kind of bug recurring.
